messages.content: Explain COBOL COPY statement and show a practical example with a copybook file and how to include it in a program

The COBOL COPY statement includes the contents of a copybook (external file) directly into your source code at compile time. It promotes code reuse and consistency.

First, create a copybook file named CUSTOMER (typically stored in a copy library):

```cobol
       01 CUSTOMER-RECORD.
          05 CUST-ID         PIC 9(8).
          05 CUST-NAME       PIC X(30).
          05 CUST-ADDRESS    PIC X(50).
          05 CUST-PHONE      PIC X(12).
          05 CUST-EMAIL      PIC X(40).
          05 CUST-CREDIT-LIM PIC S9(9)V99 COMP-3.
          05 CUST-BALANCE    PIC S9(9)V99 COMP-3.
```

Now use COPY in your COBOL program:

```cobol
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. CUSTPROC.
       ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
       INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION.
       FILE-CONTROL.
           SELECT CUSTFILE ASSIGN TO CUSTDD
               ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL.
       DATA DIVISION.
       FILE SECTION.
       FD CUSTFILE.
       COPY CUSTOMER.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 WS-EOF         PIC 9 VALUE 0.
       01 WS-REC-COUNT   PIC 9(5) VALUE 0.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           PERFORM PROCESS-CUSTOMERS.
           STOP RUN.
       PROCESS-CUSTOMERS.
           OPEN INPUT CUSTFILE.
           PERFORM UNTIL WS-EOF = 1
               READ CUSTFILE
                   AT END MOVE 1 TO WS-EOF
                   NOT AT END
                       ADD 1 TO WS-REC-COUNT
                       DISPLAY 'ID: ' CUST-ID ' NAME: ' CUST-NAME
               END-READ
           END-PERFORM.
           CLOSE CUSTFILE.
           DISPLAY 'Total records: ' WS-REC-COUNT.
```

The compiler replaces the COPY statement with the actual copybook content during compilation.
How do I use COPY REPLACING to customize a copybook for different contexts? Show a practical example with a generic record structure used for both input and output processing

COPY REPLACING allows you to modify copybook content at compile time by substituting text patterns. This enables reusing a generic copybook structure for different purposes without maintaining multiple versions.

Create a generic copybook named GENERIC-IO:

```cobol
       01 %%RECORD-PREFIX%%-RECORD.
          05 %%RECORD-PREFIX%%-ID      PIC 9(8).
          05 %%RECORD-PREFIX%%-NAME    PIC X(30).
          05 %%RECORD-PREFIX%%-AMOUNT  PIC S9(9)V99 COMP-3.
          05 %%RECORD-PREFIX%%-STATUS  PIC X(1).
          05 %%RECORD-PREFIX%%-DATE    PIC 9(8).
```

Use COPY REPLACING in your program to create input and output variants:

```cobol
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. DATAPROCESS.
       ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
       INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION.
       FILE-CONTROL.
           SELECT INFILE ASSIGN TO INDD
               ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL.
           SELECT OUTFILE ASSIGN TO OUTDD
               ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL.
       DATA DIVISION.
       FILE SECTION.
       FD INFILE.
       COPY GENERIC-IO REPLACING
           %%RECORD-PREFIX%% BY INPUT.
       FD OUTFILE.
       COPY GENERIC-IO REPLACING
           %%RECORD-PREFIX%% BY OUTPUT.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 WS-EOF PIC 9 VALUE 0.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           OPEN INPUT INFILE OUTPUT OUTFILE.
           PERFORM PROCESS-DATA UNTIL WS-EOF = 1.
           CLOSE INFILE OUTFILE.
           STOP RUN.
       PROCESS-DATA.
           READ INFILE
               AT END MOVE 1 TO WS-EOF
               NOT AT END
                   MOVE INPUT-ID TO OUTPUT-ID
                   MOVE INPUT-NAME TO OUTPUT-NAME
                   MOVE INPUT-AMOUNT TO OUTPUT-AMOUNT
                   MOVE INPUT-STATUS TO OUTPUT-STATUS
                   MOVE INPUT-DATE TO OUTPUT-DATE
                   WRITE OUTPUT-RECORD
               END-READ.
```

Benefits: Single copybook source, compile-time customization, maintains consistency, reduces maintenance burden.
What are copybook design best practices in COBOL? Explain structure, naming conventions, reusability patterns, and show a well-designed copybook example with multiple organizational levels

Copybook design best practices ensure maintainability, reusability, and consistency across applications: (1) Hierarchical Structure using 01-level groups organized logically, (2) Naming Conventions with prefixes like CUST-, ACCT-, TRANS-, (3) Comments documenting purpose and field meanings, (4) Proper USAGE clauses (COMP-3 for packed decimals), (5) Avoid hard-coding, (6) Modularity focused on single entity.

Example production-quality copybook ACCOUNTS:

```cobol
      *================================================================*
      * COPYBOOK: ACCOUNTS - Account master record for general ledger
      * PURPOSE: Used by account processing programs
      * VERSION: 1.0
      *================================================================*
       01 ACCOUNT-MASTER-RECORD.
           05 ACCT-HEADER.
              10 ACCT-RECORD-TYPE    PIC X(2) VALUE '01'.
              10 ACCT-COMPANY-CODE   PIC X(3).
              10 ACCT-ACCOUNT-NUMBER PIC 9(8).
              10 ACCT-GL-CLASS       PIC X(2).
           05 ACCT-DETAILS.
              10 ACCT-DESCRIPTION    PIC X(40).
              10 ACCT-DEPARTMENT     PIC X(4).
              10 ACCT-MANAGER-ID     PIC 9(6).
           05 ACCT-BALANCES.
              10 ACCT-CURRENT-BAL    PIC S9(11)V99 COMP-3.
              10 ACCT-PRIOR-BAL      PIC S9(11)V99 COMP-3.
              10 ACCT-YTDACTIVITY    PIC S9(11)V99 COMP-3.
              10 ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT   PIC S9(11)V99 COMP-3.
           05 ACCT-CONTROL.
              10 ACCT-STATUS         PIC X(1).
                 88 ACCT-ACTIVE      VALUE 'A'.
                 88 ACCT-INACTIVE    VALUE 'I'.
                 88 ACCT-CLOSED      VALUE 'C'.
              10 ACCT-LAST-MOD-DATE  PIC 9(8).
              10 ACCT-LAST-MOD-TIME  PIC 9(6).
              10 ACCT-USER-ID        PIC X(8).
              10 ACCT-FILLER         PIC X(50).
```

Usage in program:

```cobol
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. ACCTMAINT.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       COPY ACCOUNTS.
       01 WS-EFFECTIVE-DATE  PIC 9(8).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           MOVE 20240115 TO ACCT-LAST-MOD-DATE.
           IF ACCT-ACTIVE
               PERFORM UPDATE-BALANCE
           END-IF.
           STOP RUN.
       UPDATE-BALANCE.
           ADD 1000.00 TO ACCT-CURRENT-BAL.
```

Key principles: Clear hierarchical grouping, meaningful names with consistent prefixes, proper USAGE declarations, condition names for status values, adequate documentation, filler for expansion.

Explain DB2 DCLGEN generated copybooks. Show how DCLGEN produces copybooks, how to use them in COBOL, and the structure of generated table declarations including host variables for SQL embedded in COBOL

DCLGEN (Declarations Generator) is a DB2 utility that reads table definitions from the DB2 catalog and generates COBOL copybooks. This ensures host variables match DB2 table columns exactly. DCLGEN generates: (1) EXEC SQL DECLARE TABLE section, (2) WORKING-STORAGE host variable declarations.

Example DCLGEN output for EMPLOYEE table (copybook EMPLDECL):

```cobol
      * DCLGEN TABLE(CORPDATA.EMPLOYEE) LIBRARY(MY.COPYLIB(EMPLDECL))
      * ACTION(ADD) LANGUAGE(COBOL) STRUCTURE(EMPLOYEE-RECORD) APOST
           EXEC SQL DECLARE CORPDATA.EMPLOYEE TABLE
           ( EMPNO CHAR(6) NOT NULL, FIRSTNAME VARCHAR(12) NOT NULL,
             LASTNAME VARCHAR(15) NOT NULL, DEPT CHAR(3),
             HIREDATE DATE, JOB CHAR(8), SALARY DECIMAL(9,2),
             BONUS DECIMAL(9,2), COMM DECIMAL(9,2) ) END-EXEC.
       01 EMPLOYEE-RECORD.
           05 EMPNO              PIC X(6).
           05 FIRSTNAME           PIC X(12).
           05 FIRSTNAME-LEN       PIC S9(4) COMP-5 VALUE +12.
           05 LASTNAME            PIC X(15).
           05 LASTNAME-LEN        PIC S9(4) COMP-5 VALUE +15.
           05 DEPT                PIC X(3).
           05 HIREDATE            PIC X(10).
           05 JOB                 PIC X(8).
           05 SALARY              PIC S9(7)V99 COMP-3.
           05 BONUS               PIC S9(7)V99 COMP-3.
           05 COMM                PIC S9(7)V99 COMP-3.
       01 EMPLOYEE-RECORD-IND.
           05 EMPNO-IND           PIC S9(4) COMP-5.
           05 FIRSTNAME-IND       PIC S9(4) COMP-5.
           05 LASTNAME-IND        PIC S9(4) COMP-5.
           05 DEPT-IND            PIC S9(4) COMP-5.
           05 SALARY-IND          PIC S9(4) COMP-5.
```

Using DCLGEN copybooks in COBOL:

```cobol
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. EMPQUERY.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
           EXEC SQL INCLUDE SQLCA END-EXEC.
       COPY EMPLDECL.
       01 WS-SEARCH-ID PIC X(6).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           ACCEPT WS-SEARCH-ID.
           MOVE FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(WS-SEARCH-ID) TO EMPNO.
           EXEC SQL
               SELECT EMPNO, FIRSTNAME, LASTNAME, SALARY, DEPT
               INTO :EMPNO:EMPNO-IND, :FIRSTNAME:FIRSTNAME-IND,
                    :LASTNAME:LASTNAME-IND, :SALARY:SALARY-IND,
                    :DEPT:DEPT-IND
               FROM CORPDATA.EMPLOYEE
               WHERE EMPNO = :EMPNO
           END-EXEC.
           EVALUATE SQLCODE
               WHEN 0
                   DISPLAY 'Employee: ' FIRSTNAME ' ' LASTNAME
                   DISPLAY 'Department: ' DEPT
                   DISPLAY 'Salary: $' SALARY
               WHEN 100
                   DISPLAY 'Employee not found'
               WHEN OTHER
                   DISPLAY 'SQL Error: ' SQLCODE
           END-EVALUATE.
           STOP RUN.
```

Benefits: Host variables match DB2 table definitions exactly, includes indicator variables for nullable columns (VARCHAR length indicators), generated at DB2 catalog time so always synchronized, reduces type mismatch errors.

Show common COBOL copybook patterns used in production mainframe systems. Include examples of: nested structures, occurs clauses, level groups, and demonstrate how to use them together in a realistic transaction processing program

Production copybooks use sophisticated patterns: (1) Nested Group Structures organizing hierarchically, (2) OCCURS clause for arrays, (3) Redefines for alternate views, (4) Level groups separating concerns.

Production copybook TRANSPROC for transaction processing:

```cobol
      * COPYBOOK: TRANSPROC - Transaction processing with line items
       01 TRANSACTION-PACKAGE.
           05 TRANS-HEADER.
              10 TRANS-SEQUENCE     PIC 9(10) COMP-3.
              10 TRANS-TYPE         PIC X(3).
                 88 TRANS-DEBIT     VALUE 'DEB'.
                 88 TRANS-CREDIT    VALUE 'CRE'.
              10 TRANS-DATE-YYYMMDD PIC 9(8).
              10 TRANS-TIME-HHMMSS  PIC 9(6).
           05 BATCH-CONTROL.
              10 BATCH-ID           PIC 9(8).
              10 BATCH-ITEM-COUNT   PIC 9(4) VALUE 0.
              10 BATCH-TOTAL-AMT    PIC S9(13)V99 COMP-3.
           05 SOURCE-ACCOUNT.
              10 SOURCE-ACCOUNT-NO  PIC 9(12).
              10 SOURCE-AVAILABLE   PIC S9(13)V99 COMP-3.
           05 DEST-ACCOUNT.
              10 DEST-ACCOUNT-NO    PIC 9(12).
              10 DEST-CREDIT-AVAIL  PIC S9(13)V99 COMP-3.
           05 LINE-ITEM-TABLE.
              10 LINE-ITEM-COUNT    PIC 9(3) VALUE 0.
              10 LINE-ITEMS OCCURS 999 TIMES INDEXED BY ITEM-IDX.
                 15 LINE-ITEM-SEQ   PIC 9(3).
                 15 LINE-ITEM-CODE  PIC X(10).
                 15 LINE-ITEM-DESC  PIC X(40).
                 15 LINE-ITEM-QTY   PIC 9(7)V99 COMP-3.
                 15 LINE-ITEM-RATE  PIC 9(7)V99 COMP-3.
                 15 LINE-ITEM-AMNT  PIC S9(13)V99 COMP-3.
           05 TRANSACTION-STATUS.
              10 TRANS-STATUS       PIC X(1).
                 88 TRANS-PENDING   VALUE 'P'.
                 88 TRANS-APPROVED  VALUE 'A'.
              10 TRANS-ERROR-CODE   PIC X(4).
```

Production program using all patterns:

```cobol
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. TRANPROCESS.
       ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
       INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION.
       FILE-CONTROL.
           SELECT TRANS-INPUT ASSIGN TO TRANDD
               ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL.
       DATA DIVISION.
       FILE SECTION.
       FD TRANS-INPUT.
       COPY TRANSPROC.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 WS-BATCH-TOTAL     PIC S9(13)V99 COMP-3 VALUE 0.
       01 WS-EOF             PIC 9 VALUE 0.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           OPEN INPUT TRANS-INPUT.
           PERFORM UNTIL WS-EOF = 1
               READ TRANS-INPUT
                   AT END MOVE 1 TO WS-EOF
                   NOT AT END
                       PERFORM VALIDATE-TRANSACTION
                       IF TRANS-PENDING
                           PERFORM PROCESS-LINE-ITEMS
                           MOVE 'A' TO TRANS-STATUS
                       END-IF
               END-READ
           END-PERFORM.
           CLOSE TRANS-INPUT.
           STOP RUN.
       PROCESS-LINE-ITEMS.
           MOVE 0 TO WS-BATCH-TOTAL.
           PERFORM VARYING ITEM-IDX FROM 1 BY 1
               UNTIL ITEM-IDX > LINE-ITEM-COUNT
               COMPUTE LINE-ITEM-AMNT =
                   LINE-ITEM-QTY(ITEM-IDX) *
                   LINE-ITEM-RATE(ITEM-IDX)
               ADD LINE-ITEM-AMNT(ITEM-IDX) TO WS-BATCH-TOTAL
           END-PERFORM.
       VALIDATE-TRANSACTION.
           IF TRANS-STATUS NOT = SPACES
               IF NOT TRANS-PENDING
                   MOVE 'STAT' TO TRANS-ERROR-CODE
               END-IF
           END-IF.
```

Key patterns: Hierarchical grouping (05/10/15 levels), OCCURS for arrays with INDEXED BY for efficient searching, condition names for status values, nested structures separating concerns, COMP-3 for efficiency.
